analysis.session_summary: The tape was dominated by broad USD strength: USD was top currency at +0.363% vs majors, while AUD (-0.492%), NZD (-0.353%) and JPY (-0.157%) lagged. The main macro catalyst was the US PPI release: Core PPI actual 0.2% vs forecast 0.3%, but USD strengthened 0.153% on the event, an inverted reaction. The ECB delivered an in-line 25bp hike (2.65%) and EUR firmed 0.095%, while the press conference was muted. Brent/USD surged 6.046% and VIX rose 4.822%, reflecting oil supply/geopolitical concerns alongside risk caution.

themes.theme: Broad USD strength and commodity-FX underperformance
themes.evidence: USD mean_vs_majors_pct 0.363 was strongest; AUD -0.492, NZD -0.353 and JPY -0.157 lagged. EUR/USD -16.4 pips, AUD/USD -53.7 pips, NZD/USD -36.5 pips, USD/JPY +69.7 pips.
Brent/USD +6.046% to 108.512; VIX +4.822% to 17.75166; SPX -0.45% to 7606.4; headlines include Iran freight suspension and Trump remarks on Iran/Putin.
Core PPI m/m actual 0.2% vs forecast 0.3% (previous 0.2%), polarity inverted; own_ccy_impulse_pct 0.153; top movers EUR/USD -0.209%, USD/SEK +0.342%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD opened with a small drift lower, then a slow Asia/London recovery, but the dominant move was a 40.4-pip drop into the NY morning with Core PPI contributing 51% of that leg, followed by a late 19.0-pip bounce.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD eased early, recovered in Asia, then fell 60.3 pips into the NY morning with US PPI contributing 36% of that down leg, before a late 24.2-pip bounce.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD was nearly flat early, then sold off consistently from 20:00 to 18:45 in a 55.9-pip down leg with Core PPI contributing 25% of the move.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD fell early, bounced 23.0 pips into Europe, then sold off 50.7 pips into the close with ECB hike and US PPI contributing small shares.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY was choppy with several uncaused legs, but the largest leg was a 108.9-pip rally from 06:00 to 14:30, then a 53.1-pip pullback after ECB headlines, and a final 38.6-pip bounce.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF had an early up leg, a dip into London, then a 51.2-pip rally from 08:15 to 14:30, followed by a 14.7-pip pullback on ECB Lagarde comments.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD chopped higher overall with a high-confidence 18.7-pip up leg on Core PPI (93% of that leg), then gave back 13.5 pips into the close.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF traded within a 35.5-pip range with several alternating small legs, including a high-confidence 8.7-pip drop on the ECB press conference and a late 6.4-pip bounce.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY was very choppy with eight legs, including a 52.9-pip up leg and a 46.3-pip down leg on US PPI, ending higher on the day.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD had a sequence of alternating legs and finished down 15.1 pips, with no single clear catalyst beyond flow/technical levels.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP rose 12.2 pips over most of the session with the ECB rate decision contributing 23% of that up leg, then eased 5.1 pips late.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF traded lower overall with a final 25.4-pip down leg after ECB headlines and no single dominant catalyst.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF dropped early, rebounded 21.2 pips, then fell 23.4 pips into the close with ECB factors contributing small shares.
leg_notes.USD/SEK: USD/SEK dipped early then rallied 959.1 pips into the close, with Core PPI contributing 19% of the up leg.
leg_notes.USD/NOK: USD/NOK fell early then rallied 993.5 pips into the close with Core PPI noted but too weak to own the move.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR fell early then rallied 1919.0 pips into the close, with Core PPI contributing 17% of the up leg.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN rallied 1259.6 pips into the NY afternoon with Core PPI contributing 31% of that leg, then pulled back 406.7 pips late.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent/USD dipped early then surged 647.5 pips from 08:15 to close, with Core PPI noted but too weak to own the move.

polarity_reads.read: The inverted reaction (USD strengthened despite a miss vs forecast 0.3%) suggests the move was not data-driven but positioning or flow-driven; the market did not sell USD on a downside surprise.
EUR strengthened 0.095% despite an in-line 25bp hike, indicating the confirmation of the ECB's tightening path mattered more than the absence of a surprise.
Basket moved -0.002%, inside the noise floor; the event delivered no new directional impulse, consistent with a well-priced decision.
USD strengthened 0.042% but with no forecast to score, the move is ambiguous and could reflect policy/geopolitical headlines rather than a data surprise.

risks.why_it_matters: Brent/USD jumped 6.046% to 108.512 and headlines included Iran freight suspension/Trump Iran remarks; further escalation can lift oil and hurt risk-sensitive FX.
The ECB press conference was muted today, but further comments at 16:00 could refine the rate path and reverse EUR positioning after today's 0.095% EUR strength.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Coming window includes UK GDP m/m at 08:00, SNB Chairman Schlegel at 11:15, US Core CPI/CPI at 14:30, ECB President Lagarde and UoM at 16:00. The US CPI block is the main event; it can confirm or reject today's USD strength, while Lagarde may clarify the ECB path and Schlegel can move CHF crosses.
